title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. The boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification is a divisor with normal crossings, stratified by codimension (number of nodes). D_d is the closed stratum of codimension ≥ d and D*_d the open stratum. To a strictly decreasing flag Δ_r = (d_0 > d_1 > ... > d_r) one attaches:
- the multiplicity (stack) D_{Δ_r} and its open part D*_{Δ_r};
- 'punctured tubular neighbourhood' objects P*_{d_0...d_r};
- groupoids Π_{Δ_r} (fundamental groupoids of the D*_{Δ_r}) and Π̃_{Δ_r} (fundamental groupoids of the punctured tubular neighbourhoods), with Π̃_{Δ_r} → Π_{Δ_r}.

As the previous page explains, for fixed d_0 these form a tower of semi-simplicial groupoids, but only formally. The new non-formal structure is that the Π̃_{Δ_r} (not the Π_{Δ_r}) form a semi-simplicial groupoid as Δ_r varies.

This page. For each simplex map α : Δ_r → Δ_{r'} (218), Grothendieck wants a groupoid homomorphism α̃* : Π̃_{Δ_{r'}} → Π_{Δ_r} (219, boxed). It is to be obtained from the specialization homomorphism attached to α, that is, the map from the fundamental group of a punctured neighbourhood of a deeper stratum to that of a shallower one.

He uses the canonical epi–mono factorization of maps in Δ, so it suffices to treat surjections ('degeneracies') and injections separately. If α is surjective, the flag (d_0,...,d_r) is obtained from (d'_0,...,d'_{r'}) by repeating some entries. Then D*_{Δ_{r'}} → D*_{Δ_r} is an isomorphism of multiplicities, and the degeneracy case is essentially trivial. The next page confirms this: there the map is smooth with finite valence, and the real problem is reduced to injective α with α(0) ≠ 0, i.e. d'_0 < d_0. That case needs π_1 P*_{d_0...d_r} → π_1 P*_{d'_0...d'_r} and the map D_{d_0...} → D_{d'_0...} of codimension d_0 − d'_0.

Purpose. The goal is to encode the homotopy type 'at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. the gluing of Teichmüller groupoids along the boundary, as a simplicial diagram of fundamental groupoids of strata and their links, connected by specialization maps.
errors: Mild inconsistency: the structure is announced on the previous page as semi-simplicial, yet here degeneracies (surjective α) are also handled, which makes it simplicial. Grothendieck resolves this by showing degeneracies are trivial, so nothing is wrong, but the terminology wavers.

The direction and tilde placement in (219) (Π̃_{Δr'} → Π_{Δr}, tilde only on the source) is left unexplained on this page. The precise construction of α̃* via specialization is promised but not given here.

ideas.what: Encoding the boundary homotopy type of a normal-crossings stratification as a (semi-)simplicial system of fundamental groupoids of strata and punctured tubular neighbourhoods, indexed by flags of codimensions, with specialization maps
ideas.modern_name: stratified homotopy type / exit-path category; homotopy links (Quinn); diagram of fundamental groupoids for the Deligne–Mumford boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra appendix), Woolf; for M_g: Harvey, Harer, Ivanov, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Teichmüller tower)
ideas.where_published: Programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, structure at infinity); details only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: Reduction via epi–mono factorization of simplex maps; degeneracies induce isomorphisms of open strata
ideas.modern_name: standard factorization in the simplex category Δ

ideas.what: Specialization homomorphism from π_1 of a punctured neighbourhood of a deeper stratum to that of a shallower one
ideas.modern_name: specialization / cospecialization maps of fundamental groups (SGA1 X, SGA7 style), local monodromy at the boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1), Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group along normal crossings divisor)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for the Deligne–Mumford boundary, essentially a combinatorial model of the stratified (exit-path) homotopy type. It consists of groupoids indexed by flags of strata with functorial specialization maps, the 'link' groupoids Π̃ rather than the stratum groupoids Π carrying the simplicial structure. This anticipates the later exit-path / homotopy-link formalism, apparently in an algebraic (étale-adaptable) setting.
missed.quote: il faut introduire, pour une [application] Δ_r → Δ_{r'}, une [application] correspondante de groupoïdes Π̃_{Δ_{r'}} → Π_{Δ_r} qu'on utilise l'homom. de spécialisation associé à α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Stratified étale homotopy types (Barwick–Glasman–Haine) and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the boundary of M_{g,n} could use this explicit flag-indexed groupoid model. The idea is known in spirit, so novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step in a known programme (the Teichmüller tower and structure at infinity). The specific semi-simplicial groupoid formalism with specialization maps prefigures exit-path ideas, but the page itself only sets up the reduction to the injective case.
transcription_corrections: (219) should read Π̃_{Δ_{r'}} --α̃*--> Π_{Δ_r}; 'immersion[?]' in lines 2 and 4 is more likely 'application' or 'homomorphisme' (the next page uses 'application').
'|| qu'on utilise' is likely 'grâce à / via l'homom. de spécialisation associé à α'.
The line under 'Mais si α est surjectif' likely reads '(i.e. α un homom. de dégénérescence)'.
Margin note is at transcription '133' (archive page number), not mathematical content.
